name: Forward Linear Inclusion Function
definition: An inclusion function $[f]$ of $f$ consists of lower bound $f_-$ and upper bound $f_+$ such that $f_-(\mathbf{x}) \leq f(\mathbf{x}) \leq f_+(\mathbf{x})$. A forward linear inclusion function at $t_0$ is defined for $t > t_0$, is exact at $t_0$ ($f(t_0) = f_-(t_0) = f_+(t_0)$), and uses linear bounding lines.
summary: The Forward Linear Inclusion Function computes a conservative step size for sphere tracing by intersecting linear bounds with the zero-level threshold, ensuring no tunneling occurs.
